newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria delays ruling on agribank insolvency.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria delays ruling on agribank insolvency.

text.p: The Sofia City Court on Thursday postponed ruling on an insolvency case against the Bank for Agricultural Credit (BAC) by eight weeks due to inconsistencies in the documents on the case, a central bank official said.
"The court postponed ruling for July 11 because there were some inconsistencies in the documents concerning the bank's financial state," the official, who declined to be named, told Reuters.
Court and BAC officials were not immediately available to comment.
The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) decided to seek insolvency for BAC on January 24, 1997.

The BAC was not put into receivership prior to the insolvency bid because its activities were restricted after the BNB acquired some 52 percent of its voting shares for free in March last year and appointed a new management team two months later.
So far Bulgarian courts have declared four banks bankrupt out of a total of 17 whose insolvency has been sought by the BNB in several waves since May 1996.
Those bankrupted were the private Crystalbank, the Private Agricultural and Investment Bank, private Trade and Savings Bank and the state-owned Mineralbank.
Of the 17 banks only the private Mollov bank, now named Eurobank, avoided bankruptcy after Slovak investment fund Istrocapital acquired some 90 percent of its capital for $6.25 million.

Bulgaria's interim cabinet today approved a new draft banking law to speed up the insolvency procedure in line with a funding agreement with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), which includes introduction of a restrictive fixed exchange rate mechanism to stabilise the economy.

Under the draft, courts would be required to rule on insolvency cases within 30 days after the central bank files a suit and would not be able to appoint experts to prepare independent reports on the banks' financial state.

Delays in preparation of reports by court experts have been cited as the main reason for postponement of ruling on most bank bankruptcy cases so far. -- Roumiana Tikholova, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 911 88
